name: Health Checks
intent: Let the platform ask each instance whether it is alive and whether it is ready for traffic, so broken instances are restarted or skipped automatically, without taking down healthy ones.
scenario: A service runs as three instances behind a load balancer. One deadlocks, one is still warming up after a deploy, and the shared database has a short outage. Each situation needs a different reaction.
problem: Instances fail in different ways. A process may be running but stuck; it may be healthy but not yet ready to serve; or it may be fine while a dependency is down. If the platform cannot tell these apart, it either keeps sending traffic to broken instances or restarts healthy ones and makes an outage worse.

howItWorks.title: Liveness: is the process stuck?
howItWorks.text: The liveness check answers 'should this instance be restarted?'. It should be cheap and depend only on the instance itself, for example 'the event loop still responds'. If it fails a few times in a row, the orchestrator kills and restarts the instance.

howItWorks.title: Readiness: can it serve requests right now?
howItWorks.text: The readiness check answers 'should this instance receive traffic?'. It fails while the instance is starting up, loading caches or draining before shutdown. A failing readiness check removes the instance from the load balancer but does not restart it.

howItWorks.title: Startup: give slow starters time
howItWorks.text: Some applications take a minute to start. A startup check (or a long initial delay) stops the liveness check from killing them before they are ready, which would otherwise cause an endless restart loop.

howItWorks.title: Be careful what readiness depends on
howItWorks.text: If readiness includes a shared dependency such as the database, a short database outage makes every instance report not ready at the same moment. The load balancer then has no healthy instances, and you have a total outage, even though restarting or waiting would have done nothing. Keep readiness about the instance itself, and let circuit breakers and fallbacks handle failing dependencies.

howItWorks.title: Use deeper checks separately
howItWorks.text: A deep check that verifies the dependencies is useful for dashboards, smoke tests after deploys and alerts. Keep it out of liveness and, usually, out of readiness. Return quickly, never do heavy work in a check, and expose it on a path that is not public.

pros: Traffic only reaches instances that can serve it
Rolling deployments and graceful shutdown work smoothly
cons: A badly designed check can cause outages (restart loops, mass removal)
A shallow check can report healthy while the instance is useless
Checks add small, constant load and need sensible thresholds
They only detect what you thought to check
whenToUse: Every service behind a load balancer or orchestrator such as Kubernetes
Liveness for stuck processes, readiness for startup and shutdown
Deep checks for dashboards and post-deploy verification
whenNotToUse: Putting dependency checks in liveness, which restarts healthy instances during someone else's outage
Heavy checks that run slow queries or call many services
pitfalls: Liveness that checks the database, so a database blip restarts every instance
Readiness that checks a shared dependency, so all instances drop out together
No startup allowance, so slow-starting apps are killed in a loop
A health endpoint that always returns OK, whatever is wrong
